analytic_review: Verification, calibration, validation, outcome assessment and governance are distinct evidence claims. The error decomposition is an algebraic accounting identity and explicitly does not identify unobserved components.

Target identification is proved by feasible differences; row-space equivalence is limited to an unrestricted affine solution set and follows from orthogonality plus rank-nullity. Parameter restrictions do not become quote evidence.

Expanded cubic null direction preserves both calibration quotes. Positive prices are required only for the named request/allowed range; no global curve arbitrage or nonnegative-forward-rate conclusion is asserted.

Affine quote-error bound follows from signed interpolation/extrapolation weights; vertex perturbations attain it. Distinct tenors give identification while small gaps amplify uncertain inputs; high arithmetic precision cannot remove this economic input sensitivity.

Simultaneous instrument bounds imply the signed-book bound by the triangle inequality. Gross error exposes cancellation. Marginal standard errors are not deterministic bounds; common-source scenario arithmetic and centered random covariance examples are distinguished.

Variance/MSE decomposition follows by the zero centered sum. Conditional IID sample-mean standard error needs a sampling assumption not established by synthetic errors, disjoint IDs or same-sample demeaning. No coverage claim is attached.

The decision lower bound is conditional on simultaneous adverse discrepancy and cost bounds. A negative lower bound fails to guarantee gains but does not prove loss; a standard error cannot silently replace a sure bound.

Permission binds intended use and declared evidence. Size exceptions change only size, expire inclusively, require a distinct approver, and cannot waive numerical, scope, version, challenger or freshness gates. Identifiers and dates demonstrate policy logic without authenticating real authority.

Current dated US source context is SR26-2, not superseded SR11-7. Scope/exclusions and guidance-versus-enforceable-standards distinction are retained. All Sable thresholds and observations are original synthetic teaching choices.
